recommendations.title: Route the dashboard's primary CTA to the issue form, not the raw file editor
recommendations.description: docs/index.html line 728 (and the equivalent 'start a vote' path, line 750, already correct for opening a new file) sends a member clicking 'record your position' to https://github.com/{REPO}/edit/{branch}/votes/pr-{n}.md -- GitHub's raw file editor. No link anywhere on the page points at issues/new?template=vote.yml or template=objection.yml; the only template= link on the whole page is proposal.yml (line 798), unrelated to voting. Fix: change the href to the issue-form URL (prefilling the PR number via the form's input-id prefill, confirmed to work for input fields per the prior report's R9.3), with the raw-file edit offered as a secondary link for members who prefer it.
recommendations.conditions: Applies immediately; no dependency on any other recommendation.
recommendations.implementation_notes: Verified by grep against the live file: 'grep -n "template=vote|template=objection|issues/new" docs/index.html' returns only the proposal.yml link. Four independent reasons converge on the same fix: friction (Fogg/Norman), audit-trail consistency for the Co-Authored-By / transcription-not-decision discipline (Schneier), evidentiary uniformity for a Record Keeper's verification (Elster), and failure visibility -- the form path surfaces failed submissions via d.stuckVotes, the raw-file path surfaces nothing (Majors). Also the only route that works for the two members without push access (Scott) -- see R4.4 in voting-requirements.md. Live GitHub fork-prompt behaviour for a non-collaborator editing a protected branch is reasoned from the documented permission model, not watched live -- marked unverified in the panel transcript.

recommendations.title: Restructure the vote sub-line's visual hierarchy
recommendations.description: The .why line concatenates roughly eight clauses (headline ratio, position breakdown, awaiting list, action link, round/restart notice, yesonly warning) at one visual weight in 11.8px muted grey, with the single actionable element rendered as a bare inline <a>. Demote the repeated position breakdown to a smaller/fainter sub-line (it duplicates what the headline ratio already conveys for the common case); style the action link as a tappable button (border, padding, own line) using the existing --accent colour; keep .yesonly exactly as already fixed.
recommendations.conditions: Independent of R1; can ship in the same or a separate change.
recommendations.implementation_notes: CSS-only for the button styling; one conditional class for the demoted breakdown. Fogg's framing: a disengaged member needs three things in order -- how close, how urgent, what do I do -- and everything else is detail for someone who already decided to read further.

recommendations.title: Add a client-side, non-authenticating 'I am: ___' picker
recommendations.description: A dropdown, persisted in localStorage (reusing the existing cacheGet/blob caching patterns already in docs/index.html), that bolds or pins any row where the selected name appears in an awaiting list. Not an identity claim and not security-relevant -- it proves nothing and must be labelled as a convenience, never as 'logged in as,' so a member does not infer their vote is protected by having picked a name anyone could pick.
recommendations.conditions: No dependency on OAuth or any login system -- explicitly ruled out elsewhere (CONTRIBUTING.md: OAuth is impossible on a static page).
recommendations.implementation_notes: Fogg's own priority ranking: this is the recommendation this seat cares about most, more than the button styling in R2 -- it is the only proposed change that turns 'scan every row' into 'read the two or three that mention me,' which is the single highest-leverage ability-cost reduction available to the nine of fourteen members this seat represents. Schneier's addendum: label clearly as a convenience, not an identity claim.

recommendations.title: Consistent urgency styling for ratios, plus one glossary sentence
recommendations.description: Three structurally different ratio grammars currently render at identical visual weight: 'N toward the M needed' (affirmative threshold), 'N of M have answered... quorum N -- met/not met' (Tier C participation threshold), 'H/N endorsed' (Layer 4 endorsing reviews). Apply the already-defined, already-accessible --soon/--urgent colour classes to the ratio number itself once it crosses 50%/90% of its own threshold -- the same visual language already used for time-urgency, reused for progress-urgency. Separately, add one sentence to the existing glossary paragraph defining quorum (minimum who must respond, in any position) versus majority/threshold (how many of those must say preference) -- currently undefined anywhere on the page.
recommendations.conditions: Does not require a progress bar or other graphical element -- explicitly rejected by the panel as more build than four weeks justifies for the gain over a colour-only fix.
recommendations.implementation_notes: One function (closeCls, reused three call sites) plus one sentence of prose. This extends, rather than duplicates, the prior report's U3/U4 findings, confirmed still open on this branch.

recommendations.title: Front-load distinguishing text in form dropdowns; add the issue form to CONTRIBUTING.md's Quick Reference
recommendations.description: vote.yml's dropdown options are long single-line strings with the distinguishing clause (e.g. 'Counted as an abstention, not a yes') at the end, exactly where a skimming reader on a native <select> stops reading -- the first few words of all four options are near-interchangeable procedural language. Reorder so the caveat leads: 'toleration -- no objection (NOT a yes)' rather than the caveat trailing. Separately, CONTRIBUTING.md's Quick Reference table -- the first thing consulted under time pressure -- lists only the raw-file-edit instruction for 'Record a vote' and never mentions the issue forms exist; add one row naming them as the lower-friction alternative.
recommendations.conditions: The CONTRIBUTING.md change compounds R1 rather than standing alone -- fixing the dashboard link without also fixing the guide still leaves a member who consults the guide first with the harder instruction.
recommendations.implementation_notes: This extends the prior report's S4/D3 findings, confirmed still open on this branch (not yet fixed). Majors' addendum, folded in rather than made a sixth recommendation: add one line to the issue-closing message on a failed (5-retry-exhausted) submission telling the member explicitly to check the dashboard or file before assuming their position recorded -- a near-zero-probability event per the workflow's own code comment, so not worth new infrastructure, but worth one sentence.
